title: FOMC Minutes Timeline
html:
Newest first. Click a meeting for the full note.

MeetingDecisionRate range afterVoteKey takeaway
Sep 15–16, 2026Hike 25bp3.75–4.00%12–0Unanimous first hike of 2026; most see another hike by year-end
Jul 28–29, 2026Hold3.50–3.75%9–3 (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan wanted a hike)Hawkish dissents; markets priced a September hike; equity risk premium near dot-com lows
Jun 16–17, 2026Hold3.50–3.75%12–0Warsh's first meeting as chair; easing bias dropped; headline PCE above 4%
Apr 28–29, 2026Hold3.50–3.75%8–4 (Miran wanted a cut; Hammack, Kashkari, Logan objected to easing bias)A majority opened the door to hikes if inflation stays persistently above target
Mar 17–18, 2026Hold3.50–3.75%11–1 (Miran wanted a cut)The oil shock stalled disinflation; markets shifted to about 30% hike odds
Jan 27–28, 2026Hold3.50–3.75%10–2 (Miran, Waller wanted a cut)Mild easing bias; inflation progress "slower and more uneven"
Dec 9–10, 2025Cut 25bp3.50–3.75%9–3 (Miran wanted 50bp; Goolsbee, Schmid wanted a hold)Third cut; Fed starts buying T-bills to manage reserves
Oct 28–29, 2025Cut 25bp3.75–4.00%10–2 (Miran wanted 50bp; Schmid wanted a hold)Runoff ends Dec 1; officials sharply split on December; shutdown limited data
Sep 16–17, 2025Cut 25bp4.00–4.25%11–1 (Miran wanted 50bp)First cut of 2025 on labor weakness; payrolls revised down by more than 900K
Jul 29–30, 2025Hold4.25–4.50%9–2 (Bowman, Waller wanted a cut)Majority still saw tariff inflation as the bigger risk
Jun 17–18, 2025Hold4.25–4.50%12–0Most saw some cuts in 2025 as likely
May 6–7, 2025Hold4.25–4.50%12–0"Well positioned to wait"; tariffs threaten jobs and prices
Mar 18–19, 2025Hold; slower runoff4.25–4.50%11–1 (Waller)Treasury runoff cap cut to $5B; tariff worries rising
Jan 28–29, 2025Hold4.25–4.50%12–0Patient; tariffs and immigration flagged as upside inflation risks

Rate path: 4.25–4.50% (Jan 2025) → 3.50–3.75% (Dec 2025, three cuts) → 3.75–4.00% (Sept 2026, one hike). Also in 2025: Aug 22 notation vote approving the revised Statement on Longer-Run Goals (Fed). Back to Federal Reserve
